question: In which year, were the total faecal coliform levels from Gangothri to Diamond harbour, high?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2011**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Between Gangothri and Diamond Harbour, the Ganges River passes through numerous densely populated and industrial areas, which contribute to its pollution levels.
 
• Faecal coliform levels are a key indicator of water pollution, particularly from human and animal waste.
 
• High faecal coliform levels in a water body indicate the presence of pathogens that can pose risks to human health.
 
• In 2011, environmental studies and reports highlighted particularly high levels of faecal coliform in the Ganges River. Several factors contributed to this:
 
• Population Growth: Increased urbanization and population growth along the river’s banks led to more sewage and waste being discharged into the river without adequate treatment.
 
• Industrial Discharge: Industrial effluents, often untreated or partially treated, were directly released into the river, adding to the pollution load.
 
• Inadequate Infrastructure: Many cities along the Ganges lacked sufficient infrastructure for effective sewage treatment and waste management, resulting in direct discharge of untreated sewage into the river.
 
• Agricultural Runoff: Runoff from agricultural activities, carrying fertilizers, pesticides, and animal waste, also contributed to the pollution levels.
 
• Reports and data collected during this time indicated that faecal coliform levels were significantly higher than the acceptable limits for safe bathing water.
 
• The situation in 2011 became a point of concern for environmentalists, public health officials and the government, prompting discussions and initiatives to address the pollution in the Ganges.
 
• Thus, 2011 stands out as a year when the faecal coliform levels in the Ganges River from Gangothri to Diamond Harbour were notably high.
